newsitem.title: UK: UK manufacturing falls 1.1% in May.
newsitem.headline: UK manufacturing falls 1.1% in May.

text.p: The Office for National Statistics (ONS) released the following seasonally adjusted data on UK industrial production in May:
MINING/QUARRYING INCLUDING OIL AND GAS EXTRACTION

NOTE - Consensus forecast was for industrial production to rise by 0.2 percent in May, for a year-on-year rise of 1.1 percent. Manufacturing output was expected to rise 0.2 percent on the month and 2.5 percent year-on-year.
The ONS said between April and May, the seasonally adjusted index for oil and gas extraction fell by 2.6 percent due mainly to the early onset of the summer maintainance round.
Coal production was 3.1 percent higher in the three
months to May compared to the previous three months, but was 6.9 percent lower than in the same period a year ago.
The ONS said there were decreases in ouput in most of
the manufacturing sectors between April and May.

In the three months to May, just over half of the manufacturing sector showed decreases in output compared with the previous three months. There were decreases of 1.2 percent in the output of the machinery and equipment industries, a fall of 0.5 percent in the output of both chemicals and man-made fibres and the basic metals and metal products industries. There were however increases of 3.7 percent in the output of non-metallic mineral products, 2.1 percent in the coke, mineral oil refining and nuclear fuels industries and 1.1 percent in teh transport equipment industries.
Between April and May demand for gas and electricity increased when near normal temperatures in April continued into the next month.

In the durable goods sector, output fell by one percent in the three months to May compared with the previous three months. An increase of 2.0 percent in the output of other durable goods was not enough to offset a fall of 4.1 percent in the output of cars.
Output of durable goods in the latest three months was 1.2 percent higher than in the same period a year ago.
* biggest drop since June 1993 when drop of 1.4 percent
